l: single-source homogeneous corpus, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, opening
s: A single-source homogeneous corpus can limit retrieval coverage because it contains only one type or source of knowledge. The unit examines obstacles to retrieving knowledge from such a corpus and uses the limitations of Wikipedia-based retrieval as an example.

l: open-domain QA, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, opening
s: Open-domain question answering is used to evaluate retrieval-augmented generation and large-scale pre-trained language models. The figure reports that RAG methods significantly outperform large-scale PLMs on three open-domain question answering tasks.

l: GPT-3, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, opening
s: GPT-3 is presented as an example of a large-scale pre-trained language model and as a counterpart to RAG models. Compared with GPT-3, RAG models are described as having explicit, scalable knowledge acquisition and as easing generation by relying on retrieved references rather than generating from scratch.

l: Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 2
s: RAG is a framework that predicts an output y from a source input x by using a document reference set Z and two components: a document retriever and a text generator. The document retriever, such as DPR, narrows millions of documents to the top-K documents using relevance scores based on query-document embeddings. The text generator, such as BART or T5, conditions on the input and retrieved documents to produce y. FiD processes retrieved passages independently in the encoder and performs attention over all of them, avoiding some limitations of sequential concatenation.

l: retrieval-augmented generation methods, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 2
s: RAG aims to predict y given x and a document reference set Z by maximizing the likelihood of y. It uses a document retriever to select relevant documents and a text generator to produce the desired output, and it can seek knowledge from external information sources.

l: document reference set, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 2
s: The document reference set Z contains accessible documents, potentially numbering in the millions. The association between a document z in Z and a training tuple (x, y) is not necessarily known, although human annotations or weakly supervised signals may provide it.

l: document retriever, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 2
s: The document retriever takes x and Z as input and produces relevance scores for the top-K documents. It narrows the search space so that enumeration over the full document reference set is unnecessary.

l: text generator, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 2
s: The text generator uses an encoder-decoder framework to produce y from the input sequence and retrieved documents. A naive approach concatenates the input and support documents sequentially, but this is limited by input length and computational cost.

l: DPR, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 2
s: DPR is given as an example of a neural document retriever. It maps documents and context queries into the same dense embedding space and computes relevance as the inner product of their embeddings.

l: BART, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 2
s: BART is given as an example of a text generator that can use the input and retrieved documents to produce the desired output.

l: T5, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 2
s: T5 is given as an example of a text generator that can use the input and retrieved documents to produce the desired output.

l: FiD, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 2
s: FiD processes retrieved passages independently in the encoder and performs attention over all retrieved passages. It demonstrated state-of-the-art performance on many knowledge-intensive NLP tasks.

l: external information sources, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 2
s: External information sources provide knowledge, including texts, tables, and knowledge graphs, that RAG models can directly seek to help answer questions.

l: document, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 2
s: A document is an element of the reference set that can be scored for relevance to an input query and selected among the top-K retrieved documents. Its relevance in DPR is computed from the inner product between its document embedding and the query embedding.

l: Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: This unit proposes grounding retrieval-augmented generation across heterogeneous knowledge sources rather than relying on a single homogeneous corpus such as Wikipedia. It presents evidence that combining text, tables, knowledge graph triples, encyclopedic knowledge, and commonsense knowledge can improve open-domain question answering and commonsense reasoning. Three solutions are described: homogenizing different sources into text, using multi-virtual hops retrieval across sources, and enriching retrieved documents through structured-knowledge reasoning. The discussion concerns systems and datasets including UniK-QA, DPR+FiD, NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, and WebQuestions.

l: retrieval-augmented generation methods, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Retrieval-augmented generation is described as often relying on a single-source homogeneous retrieval space, especially Wikipedia passages. The unit proposes grounding it across heterogeneous knowledge sources to improve knowledge coverage and answer generation.

l: heterogeneous knowledge, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Heterogeneous knowledge includes knowledge from different formats, such as structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data, as well as different scopes, such as encyclopedic and commonsense knowledge. The unit proposes retrieving and reasoning over these sources jointly or iteratively.

l: Wikipedia, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Wikipedia is presented as a commonly used single-source corpus for retrieval-augmented generation. Its 22 million documents outperform the larger CCNet corpus on NQ and HotpotQA in the reported DPR+FiD comparison, and Wikipedia supplies encyclopedic facts in examples involving entities.

l: World Wide Web, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: The World Wide Web is proposed as a much larger retrieval corpus that could expand knowledge coverage beyond Wikipedia. The unit cautions that expanding to the web can introduce long-tail and quality problems.

l: CCNet, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: CCNet is described as a web-scale corpus containing 906 million documents. In the reported DPR+FiD results, retrieval from CCNet performs worse than retrieval from Wikipedia on NQ and HotpotQA.

l: NaturalQuestions, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: NaturalQuestions is identified as an open-domain question-answering benchmark used to evaluate heterogeneous knowledge retrieval. Text-only retrieval performs better than table-only or knowledge-graph-only retrieval on this dataset, while combining text and tables improves over text alone.

l: TriviaQA, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: TriviaQA is identified as an open-domain question-answering benchmark used in the UniK-QA experiments. Text-only retrieval performs best among the single-source methods, and adding tables improves over text alone in the reported results.

l: HotpotQA, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: HotpotQA is used to compare retrieval from Wikipedia and CCNet. The reported DPR+FiD score is higher for Wikipedia than for CCNet.

l: WebQuestions, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: WebQuestions is an open-domain question-answering benchmark used in the heterogeneous retrieval experiments. Knowledge-graph-only retrieval performs best among the single-source methods because many questions were collected from Freebase.

l: DPR+FiD, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: DPR+FiD is the model used for the corpus comparison and the heterogeneous knowledge retrieval results. Its reported performance shows that a larger unstructured corpus can underperform Wikipedia, while combining knowledge types can improve results on some datasets.

l: Unik-QA, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: UniK-QA is identified as one of the most relevant prior works. It retrieves information from a merged corpus of structured knowledge-graph triples, semi-structured tables, and unstructured text passages for open-domain question answering.

l: open-domain QA, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Open-domain question answering is presented as a task that can require multiple knowledge sources because some questions cannot be answered from Wikipedia alone. The unit discusses retrieving text, tables, and knowledge-graph triples for this task.

l: knowledge graph, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: A knowledge graph consists of relation triples containing a subject, predicate, and object, which can be serialized into text for unified retrieval. It can also provide explicit relational structure for multi-hop reasoning over retrieved documents.

l: tables, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Tables are treated as semi-structured knowledge that can contain information absent from or harder to extract from unstructured text. They can be converted into text by concatenating cell values by row and combining rows with delimiters.

l: text passages, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Text passages are described as the unstructured knowledge source most commonly used by prior retrieval-augmented generation systems. They can be combined with tables and knowledge-graph triples in a heterogeneous retrieval corpus.

l: structured knowledge, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Structured knowledge, including knowledge-graph triples, can provide explicit grounding and relational information. The proposed reader can reason over a query-document subgraph from structured knowledge to enrich document representations.

l: commonsense knowledge, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Commonsense knowledge contains universally recognized facts from everyday life and can complement encyclopedic knowledge. Combining it with encyclopedic knowledge improves the reported results on CREAK and CSQA2.0.

l: encyclopedic knowledge, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Encyclopedic knowledge includes sources such as Wikipedia and Wikidata and usually provides entity attributes. The unit shows that it can complement commonsense knowledge in commonsense reasoning over entities.

l: Wikidata, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Wikidata is presented as a structured knowledge source that can support reasoning over retrieved documents. In the Lovely Rita example, its relations connect the song, the Beatles, Paul McCartney, and the occupation of traffic warden.

l: T5, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: T5 is described as a decoder used by the reader model after retrieved text is concatenated with the original input. It computes full attention over the combined representations.

l: DPR, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: DPR is described as a dense retriever that can index unified text converted from structured and semi-structured data. It is also part of the DPR+FiD model used in the reported experiments.

l: multi-virtual hops retrieval, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Multi-virtual hops retrieval is proposed for cases where answering a question requires iterative retrieval across knowledge sources. It retrieves data using increasingly informed queries and seeks to determine when additional retrieval no longer provides useful information.

l: retrieval, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Retrieval is treated as a way to bridge the gap between model inputs and outputs by finding information relevant to both. The unit proposes unified retrieval, iterative retrieval across sources, and retrieval followed by structured-knowledge reasoning.

l: generation models, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Generation models are expected to use retrieved information to produce answers. Their input can be augmented by concatenating retrieved text, while structured reasoning can enrich the representations supplied to the reader.

l: multi-hop reasoning, Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3
s: Multi-hop reasoning over structured knowledge is proposed to learn relational patterns between an input query and retrieved documents. It operates on a query-document subgraph rather than the entire knowledge graph and uses a multi-relational graph encoder.

l: Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract—In recent times, Retrieval Augmented Generation
s: This study examines multilingual semantic embedding models for Retrieval Augmented Generation systems, with a focus on improving Arabic text comprehension and generation. It evaluates ten cutting-edge multilingual semantic embedding models using the publicly available ARCD dataset. Performance is assessed with the average Recall@k metric. The Microsoft E5 sentence embedding model performs best, achieving Recall@10 above 90%.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract—In recent times, Retrieval Augmented Generation
s: Retrieval Augmented Generation models have attracted considerable attention because of the impressive capabilities of Large Language Models. The study examines semantic embedding as a core component of the information retrieval process within Retrieval Augmented Generation systems.

l: Large Language Models, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract—In recent times, Retrieval Augmented Generation
s: Large Language Models are described as exhibiting impressive capabilities that have contributed to the increased attention given to Retrieval Augmented Generation models.

l: Arabic language, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract—In recent times, Retrieval Augmented Generation
s: The Arabic language is significant and widely used but has received relatively less research emphasis in Retrieval Augmented Generation. The study aims to improve models’ ability to comprehend and generate Arabic text effectively.

l: semantic embedding, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract—In recent times, Retrieval Augmented Generation
s: Semantic embedding, also called the vector embedding process, lies at the core of the Information Retrieval component in Retrieval Augmented Generation systems. The study evaluates multilingual semantic embedding models for their ability to support Arabic text comprehension and generation.

l: Arabic Reading Comprehension Dataset, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract—In recent times, Retrieval Augmented Generation
s: The ARCD dataset is used as a publicly available benchmark for evaluating ten multilingual semantic embedding models. Model performance on it is assessed using the average Recall@k metric.

l: Microsoft E5 sentence embedding model, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract—In recent times, Retrieval Augmented Generation
s: The Microsoft E5 sentence embedding model outperformed all other evaluated models on the ARCD dataset. It achieved a Recall@10 score exceeding 90%.

l: Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, I.
s: This unit introduces Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), introduced by Facebook Researchers in 2020, as a framework that combines information retrieval with language generation. It explains that RAG enables Large Language Models to use external knowledge sources, improving factual grounding, contextual relevance, scalability, adaptability, and customization. The research focuses on comparing ten state-of-the-art embedding models capable of representing Arabic language using the Arabic Reading Comprehension Dataset and average Recall@k. It also examines embedding dimension size and positions semantic embedding and information retrieval within the RAG pipeline.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, I.
s: Retrieval Augmented Generation, introduced by Facebook Researchers in 2020, combines retrieval of pertinent information from external sources with generation of contextually relevant responses. It improves the factual grounding, contextual relevance, scalability, adaptability, and customizability of generative AI systems.

l: Large Language Models, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, I.
s: Large Language Models gain access to external knowledge sources through Retrieval Augmented Generation and use the retrieved information to generate contextually relevant responses. Their context-window limitations motivate continued research into RAG algorithms and techniques.

l: Information Retrieval, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, I.
s: Information retrieval is one of the two core functions of Retrieval Augmented Generation. It selects pertinent information from provided sources, and its component is positioned within the RAG pipeline alongside semantic embedding.

l: semantic embedding, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, I.
s: Semantic embedding converts a query or context text chunk into a numeric feature vector that represents the text's semantic features. It is described as being at the heart of the information retrieval module.

l: Multilingual Semantic embedding models, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, I.
s: Multilingual embedding models have been released because many semantic models are centered on English. The research examines ten state-of-the-art embedding models capable of embedding Arabic language.

l: Arabic language, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, I.
s: Arabic language is the specific language focus of the research. The study evaluates embedding models capable of representing Arabic using a publicly available Arabic Reading Comprehension Dataset.

l: Arabic Reading Comprehension Dataset, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, I.
s: The Arabic Reading Comprehension Dataset is used as the publicly available evaluation dataset for testing ten Arabic-capable semantic embedding models. It supports the comparison of model performance using average Recall@k for different values of k.

l: Recall@k, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, I.
s: Recall@k is the evaluation metric used to compare the embedding models on the Arabic Reading Comprehension Dataset. The study reports average Recall@k for different values of k.

l: RAG pipeline, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, I.
s: The RAG pipeline is identified as the subject of Section II, where the Retrieval Augmented Generation pipeline and the positions of semantic embedding and information retrieval within it are presented.

l: Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: Retrieval Augmented Generation concerns a two-phase pipeline that retrieves relevant text from a corpus and uses a large language model to answer a user text query. Phase I: Information retrieval embeds the query and text chunks with the same semantic embedding model, indexes the chunk vectors in a Vector DB, and retrieves the top k relevant chunks. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response constructs a prompt from the retrieved context and the research query for an Arabic language model. The text emphasizes that answer quality depends heavily on information retrieval, because poor retrieval can lead to incorrect or hallucinated responses.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: Retrieval Augmented Generation uses a two-phase pipeline consisting of information retrieval followed by LLM comprehension and response. It retrieves relevant text chunks from a corpus and supplies them as context to a large language model.

l: Phase I: Information retrieval, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: Phase I: Information retrieval embeds a user text query and corpus text chunks, indexes the chunk vectors in a Vector DB, computes similarity scores, and retrieves the top k relevant chunks.

l: Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response selects a suitable LLM and constructs a prompt containing the retrieved top k text chunks and the input research query. The LLM is instructed to answer the query from within the retrieved context.

l: Information Retrieval, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: Information retrieval is described as a fundamental component of the overall process, and the system's efficiency depends heavily on its performance. If it fails to retrieve relevant corpus portions, the LLM may not find the proper answer or may hallucinate.

l: corpus, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: The corpus contains unstructured text documents. It is segmented into m text chunks, which are embedded and indexed for retrieval.

l: user text query, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: The user text query is embedded into an n-dimensional feature vector using an identified semantic embedding model. It is compared with embedded text chunks to retrieve relevant context.

l: semantic embedding, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: The semantic embedding model is used to embed both the user text query and each corpus text chunk into n-dimensional feature vectors. Accurate semantic embedding is described as important for an effective and practical RAG system.

l: text chunk, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: A text chunk is produced by segmenting the corpus, either into disjoint or overlapping segments. Each text chunk is embedded with the same model used for the query, and the top k relevant chunks are retrieved as context.

l: Vector DB, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: The Vector DB stores the vectors produced from the m text chunks. Similarity between the query vector and stored vectors is used to retrieve relevant chunks.

l: retrieved context, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: The retrieved context consists of the top k relevant text chunks returned by the information retrieval phase. It is included in the prompt given to the LLM.

l: Large Language Models, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: A large language model is selected in Phase 2 to comprehend the retrieved context and respond to the research query. The text lists open source and other models, notes that Arabic language support varies, and states that some models provide programmatic APIs at a cost.

l: Arabic language, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: Arabic language support is not available in all listed LLMs. The text identifies OpenAI GPT-turbo-3.5, Open AI GPT 4.0, Google Bard, Microsoft Bing Chat, Google PaLM2, and Jais as current Arabic LLM models.

l: generative AI, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response
s: Generative AI is described as being deployed in enterprises through this architecture for domain-specific applications.

l: Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: Research on Arabic language processing has addressed dialectal variation, text classification, and text similarity, while comparatively fewer studies have examined semantic embeddings for Arabic text. FastText, Word2Vec, multilingual embeddings, and Sentence-BERT-based approaches are discussed for word-, multilingual-, and sentence-level representation. The unit also reviews semantic embedding APIs for retrieval, Arabic sentiment analysis using multiple embedding types, and Arabic question answering through the Arabic Reading Comprehension Dataset and SOQAL. BERT-based models are reported to achieve strong results in Arabic sentiment analysis and reading comprehension.

l: Arabic language, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: Research on Arabic language processing considers the language's different dialectical nature. Studies have addressed Arabic text classification, text similarity, semantic embeddings, sentiment analysis, and question answering.

l: semantic embedding, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: The unit states that relatively fewer research studies have been conducted on semantic embeddings for Arabic text. It discusses their use in sentence-level tasks, information retrieval, sentiment analysis, and question answering.

l: FastText, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: FastText for Arabic word embeddings is described as effective. Its embeddings capture subword information, making them valuable for morphologically rich languages such as Arabic.

l: Arabic word embeddings, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: Arabic word embeddings have been generated using FastText, which captures subword information. Researchers have also explored Word2Vec-based approaches for Arabic word embeddings.

l: Multilingual FastText, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: Multilingual FastText is presented in the discussion of multilingual embeddings. The unit describes multilingual approaches as incorporating language-specific information while sharing a common subword vocabulary across languages.

l: Multilingual Semantic embedding models, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: Multilingual embeddings are used to handle multiple languages through language-specific information and a shared subword vocabulary. Cross-lingual embeddings have also been explored to facilitate knowledge transfer between languages.

l: Sentence-BERT, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: Sentence-BERT is discussed as an approach associated with sentence embeddings that capture the semantic meaning of entire sentences. Sentence embeddings have gained popularity and demonstrated superior performance in various monolingual sentence-level tasks.

l: sentence embeddings, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: Sentence embeddings capture the semantic meaning of entire sentences and have gained popularity for sentence-level tasks. Multilingual sentence embeddings have been explored for cross-lingual applications using a shared model trained for multiple languages.

l: Arabic sentiment analysis, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: Arabic sentiment analysis has been studied on social media platforms such as Twitter and Facebook. Comparative experiments using GloVe, Word2Vec, FastText, and ARBERT with BiLSTM and CNN architectures found that contextualized transformer-based BERT embeddings achieved the highest performance in general.

l: Arabic Reading Comprehension Dataset, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: The Arabic Reading Comprehension Dataset was introduced for open-domain Arabic question answering, using Wikipedia as the knowledge source. It was created from crowd-worker questions on Wikipedia articles and a machine translation of the Stanford Question Answering Dataset, and it supported evaluation in which a BERT-based reader achieved a 61.3 F1 score.

l: SOQAL, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: SOQAL is an open-domain Arabic question-answering system built to address the scarcity of labeled Arabic QA datasets. It includes a hierarchical TF-IDF component and a neural reading-comprehension component based on the pre-trained BERT transformer, achieving a 27.6 F1 score in experiments on the Arabic Reading Comprehension Dataset.

l: BERT, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, III. .. Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings, which capture the
s: BERT-based contextualized embeddings achieved the highest performance in the reviewed Arabic sentiment-analysis experiments in general. A BERT-based reader was also used in SOQAL and achieved a 61.3 F1 score on the Arabic Reading Comprehension Dataset.

l: Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, IV. .. G. HuggingFace DistillBert v1,v2
s: The unit examines multilingual semantic embedding models for information retrieval in question-answering systems, with a focus on Arabic language data. It explains how questions and context paragraphs are converted into fixed-size vectors and compared using cosine similarity to retrieve the most relevant context paragraph. The reviewed models include Paraphrase-Multilingual-mpnet-base-v2, Google LaBSE, Cohere Multilingual Embedding, Meta SONAR, Microsoft E5, and DistilBERT variants. The unit reports that DistilBERT is a smaller, faster model derived from BERT and that the study evaluated its multilingual cased v1 and v2 versions.

l: semantic embedding, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, IV. .. G. HuggingFace DistillBert v1,v2
s: Semantic embedding models encode the meaning of sentences and paragraphs into fixed-size vectors for information retrieval and related tasks. The study investigates ten multilingual embedding models with features relevant to Arabic.

l: sentence and paragraph embeddings, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, IV. .. G. HuggingFace DistillBert v1,v2
s: Sentence and paragraph embeddings represent text meaning as fixed-size vectors. They support semantic search, document retrieval, question answering, duplicate detection, clustering, summarization, recommendation, cross-lingual search, and contextual understanding.

l: Information Retrieval, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, IV. .. G. HuggingFace DistillBert v1,v2
s: Information retrieval uses semantic embeddings to retrieve relevant content even when keyword matching does not capture user intent or the meaning of extensive, unstructured collections. In the studied setting, it retrieves the context paragraphs most relevant to a query.

l: question answering, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, IV. .. G. HuggingFace DistillBert v1,v2
s: In the question-answering setting, the system receives context paragraphs, a question, and a ground-truth answer. It embeds the question and context paragraphs, then uses their similarity to identify the context paragraph most likely to contain the answer.

l: Arabic language, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, IV. .. G. HuggingFace DistillBert v1,v2
s: The work focuses on Arabic and therefore explores multilingual embedding models that support Arabic. The findings also state that Meta SONAR's claimed advantages over other models were overstated for Arabic.

l: cosine similarity distance, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, IV. .. G. HuggingFace DistillBert v1,v2
s: Cosine similarity is calculated between the query vector and the vectors of all context paragraphs. The text describes the metric as ranging from 0 to 1, with a higher score indicating greater similarity.

l: context paragraph, Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation, IV. .. G. HuggingFace DistillBert v1,v2
s: A context paragraph is embedded as a feature vector and compared with the embedded question. The paragraph with the highest similarity is assumed to be the one most likely to contain the answer.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Abstract
s: This paper studies review generation from user ID, product ID, and rating. It proposes using references selected from a large pool of texts labeled with one of these attributes to enrich the information available for generation. The framework treats review generation as text-to-text generation and addresses reference selection without textual context and model complexity. Experiments show improvements over previous approaches on automatic and human evaluation metrics.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: Opinion mining and sentiment analysis aim to digest users’ opinions about products to support decision making. Existing methods such as aspect-based sentiment analysis and recommendation systems provide less expressive outputs than textual reviews. Review generation addresses this problem by producing reviews from attributes such as users, products, and ratings, but A2T systems struggle because attribute identifiers lack semantic information. The proposed AT2T approach augments attributes with matching reference reviews that provide inductive biases for generating text.

l: opinion mining and sentiment analysis, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: Opinion mining and sentiment analysis seek to automatically digest users’ opinions about a product to support decision making.

l: opinions, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: Opinions express users’ views toward products, but many remain unknown because users have not bought most products.

l: users, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: Users write product reviews that explicitly articulate some of their opinions, while their opinions about products they have not bought are generally unavailable.

l: product, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: The product is the object toward which users hold opinions, and product attributes can be used as inputs for review generation.

l: product reviews (Amazon Books), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: Product reviews explicitly convey some users’ opinions and can serve as reference material for generating new reviews.

l: textual reviews, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: Textual reviews provide more expressive outputs than the superficial outputs offered by aspect-based sentiment analysis and recommendation systems.

l: review generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: Review generation automatically produces review text from attributes such as user, product, and rating. It is presented as necessary for obtaining expressive textual opinions about products.

l: attributes, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: Attributes include identifiers for users, products, and ratings in review generation. Their identifiers alone do not convey semantic information, so AT2T augments them with matching reference reviews.

l: A2T (Attribute-to-Text problem), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: A2T frames review generation as producing review text from non-linguistic attribute data. Its central challenge is learning rich attribute representations from identifiers that lack semantic content.

l: AT2T (Attribute-matched-Text-to-Text), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: AT2T augments attributes with their matching reference reviews to provide inductive biases for text generation. These references can reinforce frequently reviewed product aspects and habitual user phrases.

l: references, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Introduction
s: Reference reviews provide inductive biases for generation, including frequently discussed product aspects such as plot and character and habitual user phrases such as “looking forward to the next book.”

l: Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: The unit introduces AT2T, a framework that augments review generation with retrieved textual references in addition to attribute identifiers. It proposes pseudo-supervised learning (SL) for efficient candidate retrieval and reinforcement learning (RL) to select references that improve rating accuracy and lexical similarity in generated reviews. The approaches are evaluated on Amazon Books product reviews aligned with user, product, and rating attributes. Experiments report gains in content similarity, rating accuracy, informativeness, and grammaticality.

l: AT2T, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: AT2T generates reviews from attribute identifiers while additionally using retrieved references as context. The unit presents SL and RL approaches for retrieving useful references and reports improvements in content similarity, rating accuracy, informativeness, and grammaticality.

l: SL, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: SL uses attribute identifiers for parametric coarse filtering, enabling efficient matching with constant time complexity for each instance in a candidate pool. It is proposed as a pseudo-supervised approach to expedite reference retrieval.

l: RL, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: RL trains a retrieval model to maximize rewards that include the rating accuracy and lexical similarity of generated reviews. It retrieves references based on their effect on generated reviews rather than simply selecting references with the input rating.

l: reference retrieval (AT2T), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: Reference retrieval is central to AT2T because relevant references provide useful context, while noisy references can hinder generation. The unit describes retrieval methods based on attribute identifiers and reinforcement learning rather than relying only on lexical features or reference ratings.

l: references, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: References provide textual context and introduce attribute-related information that may not be available from identifiers alone. Useful references can have ratings different from the input rating while still containing relevant rating-related language.

l: output text (AT2T), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: The output text is generated using attribute representations together with selected references. The framework can use sequence-to-sequence techniques such as attention and copy mechanisms.

l: review generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: Review generation is evaluated as a data-to-text task using Amazon Books reviews aligned with user, product, and rating attributes. The reported experiments find that references improve content similarity and rating accuracy, while human evaluations find improvements in informativeness and grammaticality.

l: Amazon Book reviews, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: Amazon Books supplies the dataset used to evaluate the proposed review-generation approaches. The dataset consists of product reviews aligned with user, product, and rating attributes.

l: product reviews (Amazon Books), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: Product reviews from Amazon Books are used to test AT2T, SL, and RL. They are aligned with corresponding user, product, and rating attributes.

l: attributes, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: Attributes in AT2T are identifiers such as user ID, product ID, and rating. They provide the structured input used for review generation and for efficient coarse filtering during retrieval.

l: rating, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: Ratings are among the attributes aligned with Amazon Books product reviews. The unit explains that matching a reference's rating to the input rating does not necessarily ensure useful rating-related context or rating semantics in the generated review.

l: lexical similarity, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: Lexical similarity assigns relevance based on word overlap, with TF-IDF given as an example. In AT2T, it is considered insufficient by itself because the input consists of identifiers and lexical similarity may not capture rating semantics.

l: rating accuracy (generated reviews), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: Rating accuracy of generated reviews is used as a target for reference selection and as an evaluation measure. RL seeks references that maximize this accuracy, and the experiments report improvements in it.

l: data-to-text generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, opening .. Augmenting context using references
s: Data-to-text generation covers tasks that produce text from structured inputs such as database tables, RDF graphs, and knowledge-base relations. Review generation is described as a relatively understudied subtask of this area.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: This unit describes AT2T, a review generation task that uses user, product, and rating attributes to generate a review. AT2T introduces references, which are reviews written by the user or for the product, and selects a smaller set of relevant references before generation. Its architecture contains REFLECT, with Coarse-Grained and Fine-Grained components, and a pretrained GEN model. The unit introduces SL-REFLECT, which uses pseudo-supervised learning to train reference-selection models when only identifiers are available, and contrasts it with reinforcement learning.

l: AT2T, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: AT2T reformulates review generation as text-to-text generation by conditioning on attributes and a set of candidate references. It uses REFLECT to select relevant references and GEN to generate the output review.

l: REFLECT, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: REFLECT is the reference-selection component of AT2T. It selects the most relevant K references from the candidate set using Coarse-Grained REFLECT and Fine-Grained REFLECT.

l: SL-REFLECT, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: SL-REFLECT is a pseudo-supervised approach for training parametric reference-retrieval models when the inputs contain identifiers without text contents.

l: GEN, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: GEN is the pretrained generation component integrated with REFLECT. It uses the selected references as inductive biases for generating review text from the attributes.

l: review generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: Review generation is formulated as producing a review from review-specific attributes and selected references. The task addresses settings in which the available inputs do not contain text contents for direct lexical matching.

l: attributes, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: The attributes are user, product, and rating identifiers, represented as A = {u, p, r}. They are provided as input to the review generation task and used to select references and generate text.

l: users, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: The user is one of the review-specific attributes. References may include reviews written by the same user or by another user for the same product.

l: product, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: The product is one of the review-specific attributes. References may include reviews written for the same product, including reviews by users other than the target user.

l: rating, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: The rating is one of the review-specific attributes used as input for review generation. The text states that reinforcement learning can help REFLECT preserve rating semantics.

l: product reviews (Amazon Books), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: A review is the output corresponding to the attributes and is represented as a sequence of tokens. Reviews from the training dataset are also used as candidate references.

l: references, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: References are reviews from the training dataset that are written by the user or written for the product. Because many references can be irrelevant, REFLECT selects an optimal subset of K references.

l: SL, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: Pseudo-supervised learning is used to construct trainable SL-REFLECT models without text contents as inputs. It is presented as one of two learning approaches for the retrieval stage.

l: RL, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, AT2T .. SL-REFLECT
s: Reinforcement learning is proposed as an alternative way to train REFLECT. It enables the model to effectively preserve rating semantics.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: This unit describes Relevance Pseudo-Supervision and the Coarse-Grained and Fine-Grained REFLECT models for selecting references relevant to an input rating and review generation. Relevance Pseudo-Supervision assigns each reference candidate a pseudo-label based on lexical similarity to a ground-truth review and rating accuracy. Coarse-Grained REFLECT uses attribute-based parametric matching to reduce a large candidate set, while Fine-Grained REFLECT uses textual encoding, attention, and cross-reference contextualization to score the remaining candidates. The unit concerns REFLECT, T2T reference selection, reference candidates, reviews, ratings, and the components used to estimate relevance.

l: Relevance Pseudo-Supervision, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: Relevance Pseudo-Supervision generates a pseudo-label for each reference candidate by linearly combining lexical similarity to a ground-truth review with rating accuracy. It trains SL-REFLECT models using binary cross entropy, and the gold review is needed only during training.

l: REFLECT, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: REFLECT selects references by first applying coarse attribute-based matching and then applying fine-grained textual matching. Its relevance scores are used to select the final K references.

l: T2T, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: T2T approaches retrieve a small set of promising references using efficient text-based matching and then rerank them using more expensive matching. The unit contrasts these approaches with REFLECT because text-based matching is not available for the task described.

l: Coarse-Grained REFLECT, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: Coarse-Grained REFLECT matches input attributes with candidate attributes using encoded attribute features and an inner-product relevance score. It has O(N) time complexity and is fully parallelizable, narrowing the candidate set to M references.

l: Fine-Grained REFLECT, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: Fine-Grained REFLECT accepts the M narrowed reference candidates and uses expensive textual input features to score them. It encodes each candidate with a BiLSTM and attention pooling, contextualizes the candidate representations with self-attention, and estimates relevance using an inner product.

l: references, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: Reference candidates are scored for relevance using lexical similarity and rating accuracy during pseudo-supervision, and using attribute or textual features during REFLECT selection. Coarse-Grained REFLECT reduces the original set of N candidates to M candidates before fine-grained scoring selects K references.

l: product reviews (Amazon Books), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: Reviews provide the ground-truth text used to compute lexical similarity during training and serve as textual inputs for fine-grained reference encoding. The gold review is not required during inference.

l: rating, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: Rating information contributes to relevance supervision through an indicator that is one when a candidate and the input have the same rating and zero otherwise. Including rating accuracy helps guide generation toward a rating-consistent review.

l: lexical similarity, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: Lexical similarity measures the similarity between a reference candidate and a ground-truth review. It is computed as the average of unigram, bigram, and four-gram BLEUs and is linearly combined with rating accuracy.

l: pseudo-label, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: A pseudo-label is assigned to each reference candidate as a weighted combination of lexical similarity and an indicator for matching ratings. The balancing factor λ controls the contribution of rating accuracy relative to lexical similarity.

l: attribute-based parametric matching, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: Attribute-based parametric matching encodes input and candidate attributes with embedding matrices and fully connected layers, then calculates relevance with an inner product followed by a sigmoid. It provides an O(N), fully parallelizable alternative to text-based matching.

l: BiLSTM, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: The BiLSTM encodes the sequence of words in each reference candidate into contextual word representations. Fine-Grained REFLECT uses these representations as the basis for document-level encoding.

l: attention pooling, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: Attention pooling produces a document-level representation for each candidate from its BiLSTM word representations. It uses an attention query derived from the input attributes.

l: Self-Attention, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Relevance Pseudo-Supervision .. Fine-Grained REFLECT
s: Self-attention further contextualizes the document-level representations of the M reference candidates. It helps clarify each reference by modeling latent dependencies across references before relevance scoring.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: RL-REFLECT uses reinforcement learning to train retrieval models to select or compose references whose partial contributions improve a generated review. It samples references, generates a review with GEN, computes a reward from the ground-truth and generated review, and adapts reference sampling using the likelihood-ratio trick. The method uses filtered references from Coarse-Grained REFLECT and keeps the pretrained GEN weights fixed. To stabilize training, it prioritizes references with BLEU-1 lexical similarity and subtracts a baseline reward from the reward signal.

l: RL-REFLECT, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: RL-REFLECT trains retrieval models with reinforcement learning so that sampled references are evaluated by how their partial contributions are reflected in a generated review. It uses filtered references from Coarse-Grained REFLECT, keeps GEN fixed, prioritizes references with high BLEU-1, and uses a baseline reward to reduce variance.

l: SL, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: SL efficiently selects references using lexical and rating similarity, but it cannot guarantee that generated documents preserve those similarities. It is comparable to RL when one document dominates all aspects, but is less effective when multiple references contribute collaboratively.

l: REFLECT, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: REFLECT is discouraged by pseudo-labels from retrieving a reference with a rating nearly opposite to the ground truth, even when other aspects of that reference can strongly guide generation.

l: references, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: Reference documents can be selected individually or composed so that different documents contribute different aspects, such as character, plot, or rating-related language. RL-REFLECT samples sets of references from a candidate pool and evaluates their aggregate contribution through generation.

l: pseudo-labels, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: Pseudo-labels evaluate the lexical and rating similarity of an entire reference document and encourage selection of ref#3 in the example. They may underestimate the importance of ref#1 and ref#2 when those documents contribute complementary aspects, and they discourage retrieval of ref#2 because its rating is nearly opposite to the ground truth.

l: lexical similarity, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: Lexical similarity is used by SL for efficient reference selection. RL-REFLECT uses BLEU-1 as a proxy for lexical-similarity-based look-ahead exploration and prioritizes references with BLEU-1 of at least 0.2.

l: rating similarity, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: Rating similarity is used by SL and pseudo-labels to select references. RL-REFLECT instead evaluates rating accuracy for a generated review with a separately trained sentiment classifier.

l: Amazon Book review rating semantics, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: Rating semantics are a goal of the retrieval and generation process. Pseudo-labels can discourage retrieving references with ratings unlike the ground truth, although such references may still provide useful guidance for other aspects.

l: composing multiple documents, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: Composing multiple documents generalizes reference selection by allowing different references to contribute different aspects of a generated review. RL is presented as especially useful when references contribute collaboratively.

l: RL, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: Reinforcement learning samples a reference set, generates a review, calculates a reward from the ground-truth and generated review, and adapts sampling to maximize the reward. The likelihood-ratio trick enables gradient-based adaptation despite discrete sampling, while exploration prioritization and a baseline reduce training variance.

l: GEN, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: GEN generates a review using the sampled reference set. Its pretrained weights are kept fixed during RL training to keep the training cost low.

l: generated reviews, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: The generated review is produced by GEN from the sampled references and is used to calculate the reward. A bidirectional-LSTM sentiment classifier with attention pooling predicts its rating for estimating rating accuracy.

l: relevance score, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: The reward for a sampled reference set is computed by replacing a reference with the generated review in the previously defined relevance-score formula. Relevance scores are also normalized to form the reference-selection probability distribution.

l: likelihood-ratio trick, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: The likelihood-ratio trick enables backpropagation through the discrete operation of sampling references. It expresses the policy gradient using the gradient of the log probability of the sampled reference set multiplied by its reward.

l: BLEU-1, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: BLEU-1 is used as a proxy for look-ahead exploration. RL-REFLECT prioritizes references with lexical similarity, such as BLEU-1 no less than 0.2, because this reduces variance without substantially compromising reference quality.

l: baseline reward, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, RL-REFLECT .. Stabilizing Training of RL
s: The baseline reward is a sub-optimal reward obtained from p(X+), the reference-selection distribution. Subtracting it from the reward produces R−˜R and is used to reduce the variance associated with greedy reward maximization.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, GEN .. Training GEN
s: GEN is an encoder-decoder model with a copying mechanism for generating reviews. It encodes reference texts with a bidirectional LSTM, contextualizes and aggregates them with attention, and also attends over input attributes. During decoding, GEN combines reference and attribute representations and can copy words from references. GEN is pretrained with top-K BLEU-1 references and cross-entropy on gold reviews, while training with REFLECT-retrieved references significantly reduces performance.

l: GEN, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, GEN .. Training GEN
s: GEN uses an encoder-decoder architecture with a copying mechanism. It encodes references and input attributes, generates words with a two-layer LSTM, and can copy words from reference texts. During inference, it greedily selects the word with the highest output probability.

l: references, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, GEN .. Training GEN
s: References are encoded with a bidirectional LSTM and attention pooling, then further contextualized with self-attention and aggregated with another attention layer. GEN uses their representations during decoding and can copy words from them.

l: REFLECT, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, GEN .. Training GEN
s: REFLECT provides retrieved references for GEN, but training GEN with those references caused a significant performance drop. The text attributes this drop to even a small amount of irrelevant references misleading GEN during training.

l: attributes, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, GEN .. Training GEN
s: Input attributes are represented by embedding vectors and processed with attention to produce an attribute representation for each decoding step. They are also used to initialize the decoder through a multilayer perceptron.

l: product reviews (Amazon Books), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, GEN .. Training GEN
s: Gold reviews are used as the training targets for GEN. GEN is pretrained with cross-entropy loss on gold reviews.

l: GEN pretraining, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, GEN .. Training GEN
s: GEN pretraining uses references selected by their top-K BLEU-1 scores as inputs and cross-entropy on gold reviews as the loss function. Using references retrieved by REFLECT instead leads to a significant performance decrease.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: The experiments evaluate GEN, REFLECT, and baseline systems on the Amazon Book reviews dataset using BLEU-based content similarity and rating classification accuracy. GEN-C-F (RL) achieves the best rating accuracy and strongest human-evaluation score, while GEN-C-F (SL) achieves the highest BLEU-4 score. Retrieval improves attribute-specific content but can preserve rating-inconsistent information, whereas rating-aware relevance estimation improves both rating consistency and, in some cases, lexical similarity. Ablation results show that lexical similarity alone may fail to capture Amazon Book review rating semantics.

l: Amazon Book reviews, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: The Amazon Book reviews dataset, also used by Dong et al. (2017), contains reviews aligned with user IDs, product IDs, and ratings from 1 to 5. It is used to evaluate content similarity and rating accuracy.

l: ground-truth review, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Each review is aligned with a user, product, and rating, and generated reviews are evaluated against ground-truth reviews for lexical and rating consistency.

l: rating, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Ratings range from 1 to 5. Rating accuracy is measured by classifying generated reviews and is improved substantially by GEN-C-F (RL).

l: Attr2Seq, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Attr2Seq is a baseline that encodes given attributes with embedding vectors. Its reported BLEU-1 and BLEU-4 scores are 30.48 and 5.03, respectively.

l: REFLECT, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: REFLECT retrieves helpful reference reviews using coarse- and fine-grained models. Its references are used by GEN, and rating-aware relevance estimation improves the quality and rating consistency of the resulting generation.

l: GEN, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: GEN generates reviews using retrieved references and is evaluated with coarse- and fine-grained REFLECT models trained using supervised learning or reinforcement learning.

l: GEN-C-F (SL), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: GEN-C-F (SL) uses references retrieved by Coarse- and Fine-Grained REFLECT trained with supervised learning. It obtains BLEU-1 31.82, BLEU-4 5.65, and rating accuracy 78.93; removing rating accuracy from relevance estimation lowers these to 31.43, 5.60, and 75.49.

l: GEN-C-F (RL), Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: GEN-C-F (RL) uses references from REFLECT trained with reinforcement learning. It obtains BLEU-1 32.03, BLEU-4 5.58, and rating accuracy 84.48, and receives the highest human Best-Worst score of 11.78%.

l: RETRIEVE-C-F, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: RETRIEVE-C-F evaluates the top-1 retrieved reference rather than generating a new review. It has rating accuracy 80.33 but lower BLEU scores than the generation approaches, and its retrieved text can contain rating-inconsistent information.

l: RL, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: RL is used to train REFLECT with 50 samples per batch and to optimize rating-aware relevance. The RL-based GEN-C-F model substantially improves rating accuracy over the supervised-learning version.

l: BLEU-1, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: BLEU measures content similarity between generated and ground-truth reviews. BLEU-1 and BLEU-4 are reported, with GEN-C-F (RL) achieving the best BLEU-1 and GEN-C-F (SL) the best BLEU-4.

l: lexical similarity, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Lexical similarity is used alongside rating accuracy to estimate the relevance of references. The analysis finds that lexical similarity alone may fail to capture rating semantics.

l: sentiment classifier, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: The rating classifier is a pretrained BiLSTM with an attention layer trained on the Amazon review dataset using cross-entropy. It classifies generated reviews to measure rating accuracy.

l: Amazon Mechanical Turk, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Amazon Mechanical Turk is used to conduct human evaluation on 150 randomly sampled texts. Participants compare outputs from four systems using informativeness, correctness, and compactness.

l: human evaluation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Human evaluation compares Attr2Seq†, RETRIEVE-C-F, GEN-C-F (SL), and GEN-C-F (RL). GEN-C-F (RL) significantly outperforms Attr2Seq† and RETRIEVE-C-F at p < 0.05 using a t-test.

l: automatic evaluation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Automatic evaluation compares models using BLEU-based content similarity and rating classification accuracy. GEN-C-F (RL) performs best on rating accuracy, while both GEN variants outperform the baselines in generation quality.

l: content similarity, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Content similarity is measured by BLEU between generated reviews and ground-truth reviews. Generation models using retrieved references outperform the retrieval-only approach on this criterion.

l: relevance estimation, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Relevance estimation combines lexical similarity with rating accuracy. Adding rating accuracy improves generated-review rating accuracy and also increases BLEU-1 and BLEU-4 in the reported comparison.

l: rating consistency analysis, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: The rating consistency analysis compares models with and without rating accuracy in reference relevance estimation. Removing rating accuracy lowers rating accuracy below Attr2Seq† for both GEN-C-F (SL) and GEN-C-F (RL).

l: references, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Reference reviews are retrieved from existing reviews and supplied to GEN. They provide attribute-specific terms, but references selected without sufficient rating-semantic relevance can contain information inconsistent with the target rating.

l: classification accuracy, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Classification accuracy measures whether a pretrained rating classifier assigns generated reviews the given rating. GEN-C-F (RL) achieves 84.48%, compared with 78.93% for GEN-C-F (SL) and 80.33% for RETRIEVE-C-F.

l: Amazon Book review rating semantics, Retrieval-Augmented Controllable Review Generation, Experiments .. Analysis on Rating Consistency
s: Amazon Book review rating semantics are not fully captured by lexical similarity. The experiments show that explicitly incorporating rating accuracy helps generated reviews preserve the intended rating meaning.
